newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares in last gasp rise, seen weakening.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares in last gasp rise, seen weakening.

text.p: Ailing Singapore shares staged a minor recovery on Thursday, but the immediate prognosis remained poor, dealers said.
"This hasn't revived the market," said one dealer of the 17.83 point rise which saw the Straits Times Industrials Index close at 2,002.97.
"I don't think the sentiment is there to keep the index above 2,000," another dealer said.
Volume was low with a thin 110 million shares traded in a day which saw losers well ahead of gainers 218 to 125, with Van Der Horst faring worst of all.
The stock plunged 16 percent, losing 50 cents to Singapore $2.58 on market talk of contract delays and forecasts of poor interim results expected in the next few days.
Investors were also seen cautious ahead of the expected announcement on Friday of Singapore's non-oil domestic export and consumer price index (CPI) figures for May.
A Reuter poll of economists on Thursday saw May non-oil exports up 3.5 percent year-on-year, which would be a second consecutive monthly rise after five months of falls.
Dealers said the poll had been an encouraging sign.
